decisions.reason: The Opex decision selects a specific authorized input within the existing reference and disclosure policy; it does not change the general requirement to document assumptions or use project materials as reference points.
Selecting the original brief's operating-cost range does not change the separate site-capex assumption basis, input status, or site typologies.
The Opex basis applies to the full network but does not change its site count, typologies, authoritative site list, or treatment of missing site-level details.

The CAD-denominated Opex input does not itself change the established AUD model currency or 2031 price base; its unresolved currency treatment is already represented by the candidate's same-message ambiguity.
The operating-cost input decision does not change the debt/equity split, interest-rate assumption, tranche structure, or mezzanine treatment.
The selected Opex range does not alter the separately specified program-wide capex categories or their presentation as separate line items.
Changing the operating-cost input basis does not change which revenue streams must be modeled or the requirement to model them separately.
The Opex input may affect calculated payment amounts, but it does not change the candidate's sizing method, DSCR target, equity-IRR target, or prohibition on an inadequate DSCR-only approach.
The Opex range selection does not change the required CCA classes, depreciation treatment, tax-shield modeling, or equity-return effect modeling.
Although Opex affects computed returns, the source decision does not change the requirement to produce equity IRR output against the 16–20% target range.
The operating-cost input decision does not alter the required integrated three-statement model structure.
The Opex input can affect calculated coverage results but does not change the requirement to retain the debt schedule or produce DSCR analysis.
